claims.statement: Carrier confirmations for EXC-0921 orders arrive a median of 47 minutes after booking, while pickup slots close after 30 minutes
claims.corroboration: Observability trace explicitly measures: 47 minute median confirmation time vs 30 minute slot closure

claims.statement: Split-reservation orders created by v18 (EXC-0921 scope) are being booked with insufficient pickup slot duration relative to carrier confirmation latency
claims.corroboration: Handoff trace shows slot closure before confirmation for EXC-0921; east-node orders outside cohort booked before 05:58 succeeded; one re-booked EXC-0921 order received valid slot and succeeded. The issue started when v18 began creating split-reservation exceptions around 05:58.
claims.limitation: The specific mechanism (why v18 orders get 30-min slots vs others) is not explicitly traced, but the discriminating evidence (timing data + temporal correlation + re-booking success) is clear

dispositions.reason: C12 claimed 'carrier feed lag' but m8_r_handoffs reveals the actual issue is slot duration mismatch (30 min vs 47 min confirmation time). The lag exists but is not the root cause of the stuck orders.

next_action.rationale: Root cause (C16) is that v18's split-reservation orders are booked with insufficient slot durations. Reverting v18 (east-node reservation priority only) will stop creating split-reservation exceptions, allowing re-booking with correct slot durations. This is reversible and idempotent per the human gate scope.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Reverting v18 will prevent new split-reservation orders from being created with insufficient slots. Subsequent replay_held_allocations can re-book stuck orders with correct slot timing.
